newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves $21 million loan payment for Moldova.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves $21 million loan payment for Moldova.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund, welcoming Moldovan progress in strengthening economic reforms, said it had approved the disbursement of a $21 million tranche of a three-year loan to the former Soviet republic.
An IMF statement said the disbursement brought total IMF financial support to Moldova to $255 million.

"The IMF Executive board welcomed the recent strengthening of economic reform efforts, as reflected in the authorities' economic reform program and in the recent approval of key measures by parliament," the statement said.

"The board particularly welcomed such key structural measures as adjustment of energy prices...and approval by the government of debt restructuring and demonopolization plans for the energy sector, reform of the bankruptcy law and progress in initiating land reform."

The statement said an IMF mission would arrive in the Moldovan capital Chisinau next Wednesday for further discussions on economic policy. Deputy IMF Managing Director Shigemitsu Sugisaki would join the talks for two days.

The IMF suspended payments on its $195 million three-year Moldovan loan in the second half of last year amid concern about economic policy. Chisinau resident representative Mark Horten said in April that the IMF hoped to resume disbursements in the second half of this year.
